title: Conversational workspace, onboarding and the LLM-driven app shell
brief:
**You design the front door: "Talk to VP", the Operator, onboarding, Today and the app shell.**

**Decide:**
1. The thread-plus-cards model: card types (plan, diff, launch, call, chart, approval, issue, receipt), how a plan is shown, approved and undone, and how voice input in Hinglish works (and whether VP answers aloud).
2. The tool registry: one tool per dashboard action, risk classes (read, draft, test, external, spend, destructive, policy) mapped to autonomy A0-A3, role checks, and the "what VP did" ledger.
3. Onboarding: hear it first, sign up, say the job, company context with evidence spans, voice by ear, browser call, list, real ring. Targets: browser call under 3 min, first Indian ring 15 min or less (W7), self-serve in 30-60 min (req-39). A checklist rail that never covers content.
4. Today: the brief, approval and issue priority, empty states that teach one action.
5. The shell: left rail, a page-aware docked panel, deep links, phone layout, page edits echoed into the thread.
6. Operator brain choice (req-16): a curated list with measured latency and cost for operator tasks; predicates and permissions never depend on the model.
7. Operator conduct: asks only questions that change the call, never invents a number, shows the object page when unsure, speaks in the client's language.

**Spine constraints:** P1, P5, P7, P8; invariants 1-4; the chat-page contract (§7); no click creates or publishes; every disabled action names its fix; chat never holds configuration; launch, publish, spend and delete need A2; a model-emitted "approved" means nothing (HV law 12).

**Benchmarks to beat:** Sarvam Genie (prompt-box hero, docked copilot that builds, deploys and runs campaigns: the nearest to W10's kill bar); Retell Conductor (per-setting diffs a human accepts, page-aware chips, a 7-step checklist with locked steps); ElevenLabs Architect (go-live checklist, branch then merge; Alpha, free only through October 2026); Vapi Composer (in every header, but no REST surface); Bolna Ask Bolna (reads and writes). Avoid: Vapi's repeating welcome wall, Retell's stale tour and checklist over the canvas, Exotel's three shells, Bolna's banners taking about 90 px of 720.

**Proof:** T1 by chat with 0 silent drops, then T2-T6 by chat only (W10); 5-user sessions against incumbent captures; minutes to first call from product events.

**Owner requirements:** req-13, req-14, req-15, req-16, req-17, req-37, req-38, req-39, req-40, req-44, req-68 (provenance shown without friction).

**Lean on digests:** retell, sarvam, elevenlabs, vapi, bolna, owner-requirements-catalogue, vp-existing-assets.

title: Agent brain and human voice
brief:
**You design the call itself: brief, brain, ears, voice, turn-taking, the reply door and how she ends.**

**Decide:**
1. Architecture: a gated cascade (ears, brain, reply door, TTS) as the floor (HV law 25). Speech-to-speech only as a premium stack after a 200+ turn gate-violation battery (Gemini Live's transcript came with or before audio on 1,041/1,041 turns, but 3.8 Live talked over callers on 42% [M]). Curated presets plus an expert picker; the default after round-2 human ratings; a second voice path ready (MAI-Voice first audio 425 ms [M]).
2. Brief schema: generalise brief v2 (voicelab/server/persona_v2.py) from four hard-coded scenarios to per-agent configuration: script and identity first, safety, must-fire counts last; per-agent ledger patterns derived at publish, frozen and reviewed; a lint for recitable lines; a throwing budget.
3. Turn-taking: pause-aware release, withdraw, heard-text truncation, Hinglish acknowledgement, stop and backchannel lists, never discard "haan/nahi/ruko/bas", listen during the opening, an elderly preset, a silence ladder, an echo-safe front end (Taxila: 0/66 false barge-ins [M]); target 5% cut-ins or less at p50 1.2 s; a panel in ms with a predicted gap.
4. Speed: India media edge, warm pools, the opening rendered during the ring, number-safe clause streaming, region pinning (gpt-4.1-mini in South India: first token 304 ms [M]), effort none, a cached byte-stable core, quota per call (13-25k TPM [M]); speculative release only with a negation-aware matcher.
5. Expression: read the person (hurried, worried, irritated, chatty) in code; tone notes mapped to TTS styles, never spoken; sound tags only on Gemini voices; rate control; per-locale number reading; aap with plural verbs; less warmth on complaints and collections.
6. Reply door: one light disclosure, never denied; crisis lines; promotion fence; amounts only from data; no OTP or payment; hang-up guard; voicemail and IVR with an Indian operator lexicon.
7. Languages: Hinglish (code-mixed) default, Hindi, Indian English, regional plus English; refuse a voice that mismatches the agent language.

**Benchmarks:** ElevenLabs (3% collisions but p50 3.75 s; "haan" answered "are you still there" 4/16 [M]); Vapi (35% collisions, Gujarati on 17/18 Hinglish turns [M]); Bolna barge-in recovery code to adopt, its 500 + 900 ms hold and discarded short replies to beat; Sarvam (language hold 38/40 but p50 3.1 s, cut into the elderly pause 2/2, claimed human 6/6 [M]); Ultravox demo p50 1.54 s, barge-in 6/6. 0 of 6 dashboards show a predicted gap or a Hindi lexicon.

**Known gaps:** 15-42% cut-ins on every VP stack; a quiet "hmm" never transcribed; no human round 2; no handset timing; Gemini 3.1 Live ends 2026-11-17.

**Proof:** W3, W4, W5, KC6, T9c, blind ear tests and the listener panel.

**Owner requirements:** req-01 to req-09, req-11, req-12, req-47, req-49, req-52, req-53, req-54.

**Lean on digests:** call-quality-voice-turn-taking-2026-10-21 (primary), vp-existing-assets, elevenlabs, bolna, sarvam, vapi, retell, owner-requirements-catalogue.

title: The campaign engine end to end, including data intake
brief:
**You design how a list becomes calls, and how calls become follow-through.**

**Decide:**
1. The campaign object and state machine (draft, ready, scheduled, running, paused, completed, cancelled, recurring) with a category-first form: service, transactional or promotional sets the window and number series. Fields with defaults on: consent source, DND status, retry ladder by outcome (busy, no answer, failed, short call, voicemail, provider error), attempt budget per contact per day and week, pacing with reserved inbound capacity, a compliant caller-ID pool, predial (built-in plus an optional customer veto), budget and estimate, follow-ups (WhatsApp utility, DLT SMS, callback, human hand-off), local-time windows, holidays, windows across midnight, resume after an outage.
2. Intake: CSV, XLSX, Sheets and API push; the CSV contract shown before upload; AI column mapping with review; India-default E.164; cross-format and cross-script dedupe; a reason per row; a failed-rows file; never reject a whole file; counters for rejected, duplicate, DND and consent; per-row overrides (language, voice, variables); a test call to one row.
3. Attempt separate from call; precheck reasons; carrier codes kept; one dial path for campaign, API, single, test, retry and callback.
4. Inbound: number to agent, caller lookup, after-hours behaviour.
5. Presets: insurance renewal (inform, confirm, hand off; IRDAI pack), lending pre-due (RBI-ready logs), appointment and subscription reminders.
6. The launch card, and a disabled Launch that names the blocker and links to it.

**Spine constraints:** P6, P7, P9; invariants 1, 5, 6; W1 and W2; tasks T2, T3, T9b; the messy-50 spec (research/2026-10-20/teardown/synthesis/messy-50.spec.json). Test lists must never ring strangers (risk.2026-10-20.synthesis-test-list-dials-strangers).

**Benchmarks:** Sarvam (retry ladder by outcome, rejected-records file, attempt and interaction split, 0.1-500 attempts per second, commit gate in the wizard); Bolna (row codes, +91 default, 150,000 rows, nodes that state their contract); ElevenLabs (CSV contract before upload, per-row overrides); Retell (multi-range windows with days, reserved-concurrency readout); Exotel (transactional vs promotional, retries 0-3, throttle); SquadStack (one canvas for bot, human, SMS with DLT fields). Beat: 0 of 6 forms carry compliance; Retell 00:00-23:59 default and no retries; Vapi's dashboard code prepends + to a 10-digit number, it has one absolute window and it did not retry outage calls; ElevenLabs has one start time; Bolna has two outbound systems; Synthflow cancels after 7 days.

**Proof:** T2 48/50 rows in under 5 min; T3 refuses a promotional call at 09:30; 0 rings on opt-out rows, across campaigns.

**Owner requirements:** req-17, req-19, req-20, req-21, req-23, req-24, req-28, req-65, req-66.

**Lean on digests:** sarvam, bolna, elevenlabs, retell, vapi, exotel, synthflow-squadstack, blueprint-lane-market-regulation-money-2026-10-21, owner-requirements-catalogue.

title: Per-call and campaign AI analysis, live mission control, reporting
brief:
**You design how the client sees and understands every call and every campaign.**

**Decide:**
1. The call page: stereo player; transcript in native script, romanised and translated, ordered by audio offset (HV law 29); turn timeline with latency segments and heard text; run manifest; compliance trace; cost lines.
2. Outcomes: client-owned outcome definitions in business language; default judges (summary, success, sentiment) created visible and editable (Bolna hides its auto-judges); pinned judge models; classification against verified keys, with agreement to CRM truth measured before any label is trusted (a 90%-accurate label inflates sample needs 1.8-2.4x [C]).
3. Failure explanation: engineering reason, carrier code, a business-language reason and a next action, including Indian causes (DND, CLI or DLT rejection, operator announcement, window).
4. The campaign view: funnel with a reason at each drop; cost per outcome; drivers by segment, hour and number; a line-hazard ribbon (hang-ups aligned to TTS clauses); objection clusters with quotes; best and worst calls; "observed, not causal" and "under-powered" labels.
5. Mission control: live calls, concurrency, listen, whisper, take over (audited); Supervisor alerts for loops, anger and crisis words; issues with severity, calls impacted and time to resolve; never "all good" without monitors.
6. Q&A: answers with quotes and play-from-here, numbers from the same queries as pages.
7. Reports and export: daily brief; scheduled reports; one export per campaign with outcome, fields, transcript, recording link and cost (T6); signed webhooks; CRM write-back.
8. Distinct empty, zero, loading and failed states; sample data labelled.

**Benchmarks:** Vapi (log tabs, issues with severity and MTTR and a Compliance category, structured outputs feeding scorecards, per-turn latency; but 638 raw end codes and "Great news" with no monitors); Retell (13-column call history with cost, latency and outcome, live take-over, context injection, AI QA; but unlabelled sample data); ElevenLabs (12 analytics tabs, honest "---" empties, a charging block per call); Sarvam (collections disposition model, self-QA flags, SQL boards); Exotel (sentiment-crash alerts, a version column in logs); Synthflow (SIP ladder and MOS per leg). 0 of 5 group cost by campaign or contact; SquadStack searches only 10 days.

**Proof:** T5: five induced failures, each found in under 60 s, 5/5 correct, 4+ actionable (W6); T6 export 6/6; judge agreement against verified keys.

**Owner requirements:** req-21, req-22, req-25, req-26, req-27, req-45, req-46.

**Lean on digests:** vapi, retell, elevenlabs, sarvam, exotel, synthflow-squadstack, blueprint.learning-memory-omnichannel, owner-requirements-catalogue.

title: Memory, personalisation and omni-channel data
brief:
**You design how VP knows the person and the company, and what it may remember.**

**Decide:**
1. The model beyond the spine's objects: Episode (call, chat, WhatsApp, email), Fact (preference, commitment, objection, stated fact, correction, opt-out; exact caller quote with episode and span; source and authority rank; expiry; purpose; consent; status), Commitment, PreferenceView and the MemoryBrief compile policy (approved, purpose-matched facts only; newest supported wins; whole entries; a byte cap; a middle slot; a throwing budget).
2. The write path: the extractor proposes facts that cite an exact caller quote, re-checked at commit; a refusal guard ("no follow-up please" never creates one); tiers: opt-out applies at once, language, pace and register auto-apply with undo, commitments and money facts need review. Never store the agent's own claims, brief facts, mood or personality scores.
3. Recall: semantic plus keyword legs (lexical recall alone recovered 0/27 adversarial cases [M]); injection through the pre-call hook; memory must not push p50 above 1.2 s; multi-call simulations and a live adherence test (an inherited trial stored "Hindi" and replied in English [M]).
4. Omni-channel intake and what to take: CSV and Sheets; CRMs (LeadSquared, Zoho, Kylas, Salesforce; build when two paying customers need one); API push for speed-to-lead; WhatsApp in the 24 h window (Meta terms bar training on its data); DLT SMS; email; app events with consent; payments (outcomes; "link opened" as a leading indicator); policy and loan systems (highest authority); documents and website for the company brain, kept apart from contact memory.
5. Identity: exact match only, no fuzzy merge; unverified channel senders produce feedback, never memory.
6. DPDP: tenant is fiduciary, VP is processor; purpose and basis per fact; retention classes; forget follows the person, with a tombstone; India region; no cross-tenant pooling.
7. Surfaces: contact timeline, facts with quotes and play-from-here, edit and forget, "what she remembers" settings, memory cost at the toggle.
8. Phasing: preference memory in late v1 (Plus) or v2.

**Benchmarks:** Retell (a 2,000-character rewritten brief per phone number, read on, save off, USD 0.005 per run, a sane update prompt); Synthflow (summaries shared across voice, SMS and WhatsApp, keyed by phone); ElevenLabs (built, gated, keyed to a browser fingerprint); SquadStack (memory claimed, code intra-call only); Bolna, Sarvam, Vapi, Exotel (none). Reuse Relay's evidence-span intake and AI column mapping as concepts.

**Kill criteria:** recall under 95%, preferences ignored more than 1 in 20, or p50 above 1.2 s (`decision.2026-10-19.tier-plus`).

**Owner requirements:** req-10 (accent as opt-in personalisation, not a wedge), req-12, req-28, req-29, req-30, req-31, req-32, req-33 (groups only as consented aggregates).

**Lean on digests:** blueprint.learning-memory-omnichannel (primary), retell, synthflow-squadstack, elevenlabs, vp-existing-assets, blueprint-lane-market-regulation-money-2026-10-21, owner-requirements-catalogue.

title: The self-learning system
brief:
**You design how VP gets better from its own calls without fooling anyone, the client included.**

**Decide:**
1. What is learnable, at which level and volume: turn-taking parameters (dense; cut-ins 25% to 18% need about 70-165 calls per arm, ICC assumed [C]); the opening slot after the locked disclosure; line-level drop-off (the owner's call 100 to call 101); best time inside the legal window; objection handling; brief wording in middle slots; voice per segment (panel); business outcomes (slow: 6,510 calls per arm for 20% to 22% [C]). Never learned: disclosure, consent and opt-out, crisis lines, identity, prices, offers and dates, the category fence, rules appended last.
2. The pipeline: measure in code; propose, probe and compose offline (invariant and domain candidates, simulated callers with hidden keys, repeated runs, contrasts measured in code, each merge citing an observation); gates (one compile, shape lint, budget, empty diff on locked sections, no new number or identifier, India latency budget); one-tap approval; online proof on a fixed horizon (a line fix is proved in about 592 calls per arm on local hazard vs 25,963 on conversion [C]); expiry at 60-90 days or on drift; per-tenant and invariant-lesson libraries with no personal data.
3. Statistics as code: per-tenant A/A; pre-registration; fixed-horizon or always-valid tests; effects from held-out data; discounted Thompson only from about 1,000 calls a day on one script; guardrail auto-stop (opt-outs, complaints, disclosure adherence, early hang-up per CLI under TRAI reg 21A, minutes rising without outcome change, empty ASR).
4. A fast lane for catastrophic lines like the owner's 90-of-100 example, visible within tens of calls [I]: proposal, approval, then measurement.
5. Surfaces: learning-inbox cards (problem, diff, contrasts, calls to prove), an experiments page with a power meter and "under-powered: N more calls", and the "how she changed for you" timeline with intervals.
6. Copy rules: "remembers every customer, shows where calls fail, proves the changes you approve", never "learns on its own" below volume.
7. Pricing interplay: anything correlated with minutes is learned only under outcome or seat pricing.

**Benchmarks:** Retell Conductor (failed calls become tests; human-accepted diffs; fixed-weight A/B without statistics); ElevenLabs Architect (branch, merge, manual promotion); Vapi (monitors, simulations, splits without statistics; Composer can bypass approvals); SquadStack Lift, claimed (locked sections, staged rollout, significance flag); Bland's autonomous loop. None documents A/A, sample size, stopping or expiry.

**Evidence to respect:** two-arm daily dashboards gave 52-62% false winners; pooled learning gave the wrong winner to 48-55% of dissimilar tenants; harness2's gains are vendor-claimed, on document tasks, with no human gate.

**Owner requirements:** req-27, req-33, req-34, req-35, req-36.

**Lean on digests:** blueprint.learning-memory-omnichannel (primary), retell, elevenlabs, vapi, synthflow-squadstack, call-quality-voice-turn-taking-2026-10-21, owner-requirements-catalogue.

title: India telephony, numbers, compliance, safety, security and governance
brief:
**You design the rails and the rules: what may be dialled, from which number, saying what, and who can see it.**

**Decide:**
1. Telephony: bring-your-own carrier with numbers in the tenant's name (Plivo primary, Exotel AgentStream, Vobiz); VP never connects PSTN calls itself; a trial line for browser and verified-number tests (missed-call check; caller ID can be spoofed); India media edge; pulses of 30 s or less; carrier failover; answering-machine detection on Indian announcements; cold, warm and agentic-warm transfer with a spoken brief; DTMF; CNAP trade name.
2. The number step: series by category and sector (140xx promotional; 1600xx for RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA service calls; 1601xx utilities and logistics; declared 10-digit otherwise); KYC documents, time and price before any credential; number health against TRAI reg 21A flags; the A2P CLI-range declaration export (due about 2026-11-17/18); 1600 price and streaming unknown (KC5).
3. The compliance core: M1 category classifier and in-call promotion fence; M2 series routing, A2P export, health; M3 windows (promotional 10:00-21:00; a humane service default; RBI 08:00-19:00 from 2027-01-01; contact local time); M4 suppression on every path, in-call opt-out, attempt caps; M5 consent ledger (wave 2); M6 DPDP Rule 3 notice by link after the call, recording notice, retention, residency; M7 sector packs (IRDAI inform, confirm, hand off with 10-year India records; RBI logs). Never market NCPR scrubbing.
4. Reply-door safety: one light disclosure, never denied; refuse prompts that tell the agent to claim to be human (T9c); crisis lines; no OTP or payment; anti-scam design (verifiable callback, links on the client's domain, no refund or bonus framing).
5. Security and governance: fixed roles on every plan; audit log; scoped API keys with expiry and spend caps; widget keys closed by default; PII redaction (Aadhaar, PAN, bank, card) on; retention chosen at onboarding; India region by default; telemetry masked and kept in India; a tenant-isolation leak battery.
6. Liability: tenant is Sender and Data Fiduciary, VP a processor; counsel list: renewal solicitation (KC8), sender status, recovery agency.

**Benchmarks:** Exotel (140, 1600 via a VNO, call-type field; bot path off by default); Bolna (Truecaller check, KYC list before the click; wrong 9-21 window); Sarvam (rent and BYO side by side; 10-digit only, DND by API, session replay set to a US host); Retell (ID wall, DNC off and skipped by batch, no Aadhaar or PAN redaction); ElevenLabs (open-allowlist warning; Singapore default under +91); Vapi (the only predial veto; no Indian path); SquadStack (in-call dnd_request, DLT fields; avoid spam-number rotation); Synthflow (opt-out judge failed silently for 2 h 50 m).

**Proof:** W1 (0 rings on opt-out rows, across campaigns); T3; T9a promotion fence; T9c 0 denials; A2P export before launch.

**Owner requirements:** req-47, req-48, req-49, req-55, req-65, req-67.

**Lean on digests:** blueprint-lane-market-regulation-money-2026-10-21 (primary), exotel, bolna, sarvam, retell, elevenlabs, vapi, synthflow-squadstack, owner-requirements-catalogue.

title: Cost, pricing, speed, architecture, APIs, integrations, reliability and learning from competitors
brief:
**You design what VP costs, how fast and reliable it is, how others build on it, and how it keeps learning from the market.**

**Decide:**
1. Pricing: the unit (all-in per connected second incl. telephony and GST, pulse stated); tiers (Base human voice; Plus memory and learning inbox; Premium personalisation and a dedicated voice), re-priced after the default stack; per-outcome only for managed design partners; no setup fees; caps per workspace and API key; a pre-launch estimate; UPI or card wallet, invoice and NEFT above the INR 15,000 e-mandate cap, GST and TDS; low-balance and overdrawn states; refund rules. Never trade voice for price (req-02).
2. The INR 2 path: AI cost per minute by stack (gated cascade 0.94 [M]; Gemini-TTS hybrid 0.98, 1.34 from 2027 [I]; all-Gemini 1.56, then 1.92; Live 4.2-5.7 at 3 min [M]); thresholds for cheaper ears and voices (about 250k-2.5M min/month); FX, the A2P charge (telcos ask INR 0.50/min) and the unknown 1600 price.
3. Architecture: the proposed split (a Python realtime voice service ported from voicelab along its seams; a TypeScript control plane on Postgres, Neon allowed); India media and orchestration; an adapter registry with measured metrics (n, date); warm pools; quota per concurrent call; HV laws 30-32 (wake then sign, every queue names its caller, 5xx classifier with deadlines).
4. Speed budgets per segment (endpoint, hold, brain first token, first audio, phone leg), measured at the handset.
5. Reliability: service levels, synthetic calls, detection and client notice in minutes, carrier and provider failover, an honest status page, resume after outage.
6. API, SDK and MCP from one spec, 1:1 with the dashboard (W10): 422 on unknown fields, idempotency keys, signed slim webhooks with retries and replay, pre-call and predial hooks, cost by campaign and contact.
7. Integrations: CRM, WhatsApp BSP, payment webhooks, Sheets.
8. The competitor radar (Scout): the 67-URL watchlist (research/2026-10-20/teardown/radar/watchlist.json): status daily; changelogs, docs, APIs, prices weekly; re-walks monthly; call battery quarterly; tripwires (India region, INR billing, TRAI or DLT in docs, Hinglish mode, memory or campaigns live, price at INR 4 or less); graph inbox entries and a monthly owner digest.

**Benchmarks:** Bolna's price table and cost header; Sarvam's INR rate table with UPI and GST; Retell's price at the toggle and per-second cost lines; Vapi's typed cost lines, query endpoint, config as code. Beat: headlines without telephony or wait (Vapi), burst on by default (Retell, ElevenLabs), Retell's 4,000-token multiplier, Sarvam's 60 s pulse, Exotel's quote gate; 0 of 5 cap spend by API key or cost by campaign. Reliability bar: Vapi's 4 h 07 min outage (no campaign retry), Retell's 6 h of unnoticed degradation, Bolna's 9 of 18 incidents upstream with no carrier failover.

**Owner requirements:** req-08, req-11, req-41 to req-44, req-50 to req-52, req-54, req-58 to req-61.

**Lean on digests:** blueprint-lane-market-regulation-money-2026-10-21, call-quality-voice-turn-taking-2026-10-21, vp-existing-assets, vapi, retell, bolna, sarvam, exotel.

title: Visual identity, motion, sound, tone and vibe, plus specs for the key screens
brief:
**You design how VP looks, moves, sounds and speaks, and the key screens.**

**Decide:**
1. Identity: warm, human, Indian, calm and confident, never generic SaaS. The owner rejected Relay's look three times (DM Sans, indigo, 13 px body, "Quiet Operations Desk": DESIGN.md); the best direction in the repo is /prototype's warm editorial concept (serif display, warm palette, dark green, terracotta: asset.se-live.prototype-visual-concept). Devanagari-ready type pairing, readable body size, light and dark, accessible contrast.
2. Voice-first UI: audio is a first-class element (waveforms, play-from-here, the same Hinglish line in three registers on voice cards, live listen); quiet UI sound cues for connect, approval and issue, mutable, never autoplayed.
3. Motion: only to show the system working (calls ringing and connecting, cards arriving in the thread, funnels filling, diffs resolving); reduced-motion support; a performance budget.
4. Words: plain, warm Indian English, Hinglish where the client speaks it; never auditor-style warning walls; units in ms and INR; reasons with fixes; distinct empty, zero, loading and failed states; "not measured" instead of zero; the Operator sounds like a capable colleague. Name the Operator.
5. Persona defaults with the voice module: friendly, human, professional, interesting (req-07); no companion or romance voices in a business catalogue.
6. Components: thread cards (plan, diff, launch, call, approval, issue, chart); tables carrying evidence grades; timelines; transcript synced to audio; INR and ms readouts with n and date; state tokens.
7. Key screens to specify at 1280 px and 390 px: Talk to VP; Today; the launch card; campaign mission control; the call page; the agent builder (brief editor, stack picker, turn-taking panel, docked test); contact timeline; learning inbox; number step; wallet; hear-it-first onboarding.

**Benchmarks (WT §4):** adopt Vapi's per-row latency, cost and score; ElevenLabs' description under every setting and honest empty states; Bolna's persistent cost bar; Sarvam's inline gate with the fix and native-script glyphs; Retell's plain transfer copy and page-aware chips; Exotel's version pill and live concurrency meter. Avoid: click-to-publish, silent disabled buttons, charts on no data, "0 ms" on empty data, stale tours, permanent banners, three shells, US defaults on an India path, unlabelled sample data.

**Proof:** 5-user sessions at desktop and phone width against incumbent captures (task errors, time); the owner's visual review (req-40); every screen passes the state-integrity rules.

**Owner requirements:** req-07, req-37, req-38, req-39, req-40, req-68.

**Lean on digests:** owner-requirements-catalogue, vp-existing-assets, vapi, retell, elevenlabs, sarvam, bolna, exotel.
